title: Halifax JD151 Memorial, Wressle (Intake Plantation)
location_name: Intake Plantation, Wressle, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
crew_summary: Three killed, four survived with injuries. P/O Binns and Sgt Gillicker killed in the crash; F/Sgt Brown died of injuries on 13 August 1943.
narrative: Halifax JD151 of 78 Squadron was returning from Nuremberg on 11 August 1943 short of fuel. Waiting seventh in the landing queue at Breighton, two engines cut out and the pilot lost control. The aircraft crashed at 06.19 near Bowthorpe Hall, South Duffield. Navigator Harry Binns and air gunner Thomas Gillicker died; flight engineer William John Brown died of his injuries on 13 August. The other four crew were injured.

crew.name: Richard Lewis Barger
crew.fate_detail: Survived with injuries. Died 2012; buried Saint Colmans Cemetery, Fayette, Ohio.

contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register

external_narratives.summary: Researcher's account of 78 Squadron Halifax JD151 running out of fuel returning from Nuremberg, with crew list. Says the small JD151 plaque in Intake Plantation, Wressle, is at the wrong location, two miles from the real crash site.
key_details: Crash 06.19 near Bowthorpe Hall, South Duffield
Plaque in Intake Plantation is at wrong location
Memorial photo credited to Eric Barton

community_connection: Albert Pritchard, Eric Barton and Ken Reast located the correct crash site near Bowthorpe Hall.
memorial_details: A small plaque to JD151 stands in Intake Plantation, Wressle, about two miles from where the aircraft crashed. Yorkshire Aircraft, the only source found, says this is the wrong location and suggests a mix-up at the Yorkshire Air Museum. The wood has no public right of way. The source does not say who arranged the plaque or who maintains it.
